# Inactive reconstructed CJK companion

This companion was reconstructed after the 2026-10-06 workspace reset. Version
`0.9.4+viola.cjk.4` separates the retained Japanese and Mandarin dependency
extras. It preserves the corrected `.3` pronunciation, dictionary-manifest and
notice bytes, including the established U+032F normalization restored in public
change #73. The `.2` experiments and uniquely identified `.3` artifact remain
historical evidence; their identities are not reused for the changed metadata.
No registry publication, profile activation or customer release is implied.

The English fork remains a base dependency. Install `[mandarin]` for the pinned
pypinyin/cn2an/Jieba/ordered-set/proces chain, `[japanese]` for
Fugashi/jaconv/MojoMoji, or both extras when both routes are explicitly selected.
The composition checks only the requested routes' versions, before frontend
initialization. Selecting Mandarin does not require Japanese native modules or
the external UniDic payload. All dormant Japanese source/data/notices remain
in the companion; no language implementation is deleted.

The four required official Misaki modules, `ja_words.txt`, Apache license and three inherited MIT notices were recovered from authenticated Git objects and match the previously recorded hashes. The decimal preparer was reconstructed from retained source text and matches its original hash. The authored bridge, dispatcher and runtime forwarding are new source and require fresh tests/review.

The old Japanese dictionary receipt was lost. The reconstructed official unidic-py 3.1.0+2021-08-31 input supplies eighteen exact file identities, including its unchanged notices. The factory hashes these files in 1 MiB chunks before imports, captures the canonical directory, supplies an explicit neutral configuration and the verified 29-field schema, and checks the dictionary actually selected. It never probes an ambient dictionary. Fresh 2026-10-07 Linux component runs established native Japanese initialization, bounded Japanese/Mandarin G2P and Kokoro synthesis using retained local inputs. Those dated results do not establish Windows loading, frozen application behavior or old per-file equality. See `docs/CUSTOMER_SPEECH_QUALIFICATION.md` in the source repository for the evidence and remaining boundaries.

These eight `misaki` payloads are additions to the existing `viola-misaki-en` files in one physical installed package directory. This distribution owns no `misaki/__init__.py`, `misaki/data/__init__.py`, English module or lexicon. Separate source roots do not automatically merge with the English regular package. Packaging must verify the combined physical layout and retain the English bytes exactly.

The declared dependency versions are the same previously investigated versions; this reconstruction does not install them or assert complete transitive license/native-wheel qualification. Original Apache and MIT notices are retained. The existing Fugashi/MeCab, UniDic and other dependency attribution/terms remain separate final bundle obligations. No historical fork lineage or new license election is inferred.

The first-release qualification target is English, Spanish and Mandarin.
Existing eight-family source and the complete canonical 54-voice asset are
preserved for later expansion. Asset membership does not advertise every voice:
the selected voice set still needs its own pronunciation, acoustic, frozen,
signed and installed qualification. Three representative voices are the first
test pass, not a permanent one-voice-per-language restriction. Caller-selected
voice identity and application defaults remain unchanged.
